decisions.intent: Complete a cross-block cut with one reference decision, a successful clipboard write, and one undoable removal transaction.

preconditions: A non-collapsed selection starts and ends in different editable blocks.
The selected removal set may contain referenced definition blocks.
stateTransitions: The editor derives the exact removal set and asks for reference confirmation before clipboard output.
After the approved clipboard write, removal receives that already-approved decision and performs one transaction.
outputs: A successful cross-block cut writes its clipboard representation before changing the editor DOM.
Undo receives the complete cross-block mutation rather than a partial post-copy edit.
invariants: The same reference confirmation is never shown twice for one Cut command.
The existing image, AV and table cut paths keep their independent semantics.
failures: A declined reference confirmation or failed clipboard write leaves the original DOM unchanged.

decisions.intent: Normalize copied cross-block fragments so pasted block structure retains visible block chrome and removes virtual references.

preconditions: A copy range spans block boundaries and produces a detached DOM fragment.
The source editor can contain actions, callout metadata, attributes and virtual block references.
stateTransitions: The detached fragment removes virtual-reference semantics before serialization.
For each copied block, source-level action, callout and attribute elements are restored when the partial range omitted them.
outputs: The rich clipboard output preserves copied block metadata required by later paste and undo behavior.
The plain-text output contains one normalized copied block per line.
invariants: Normalization edits only the detached clipboard fragment, never the live editor source.
A source block with no matching copied block does not add unrelated chrome.
failures: Missing source counterparts are ignored without mutating either the source DOM or unrelated copied blocks.

decisions.intent: Give copied sibling list items a uniform subtype without importing drag-and-drop transaction semantics into clipboard processing.

preconditions: A normalized copied fragment consists entirely of sibling list items.
At least one copied item declares the target subtype.
stateTransitions: The first sibling subtype becomes the fragment subtype.
Other copied siblings receive matching DOM and action chrome through a clipboard-specific conversion helper.
outputs: Pasted list fragments retain a single coherent list subtype.
Ordered-list markers are removed when the copied subtype becomes unordered.
invariants: Clipboard conversion does not emit drag-and-drop editing markers or transactions.
Mixed fragments that are not wholly sibling list items remain untouched.
failures: A fragment without a declared subtype keeps its original representation.

decisions.intent: Flatten copied nested-list roots so a cross-block clipboard fragment can be pasted as independent top-level list items.

preconditions: The copied fragment begins with a list item whose only block child is a nested list.
That nested list contains one or more list items.
stateTransitions: The wrapper list item is replaced with its nested list items in the detached fragment.
The resulting sibling list items are then normalized to one subtype.
outputs: The copied fragment exposes the selected nested list items at its top level.
The rich and plain-text clipboard formats describe the same normalized selection.
invariants: Only a structurally exact nested-list root is flattened.
Live editor nesting and unrelated copied child blocks are preserved.
failures: Empty or structurally mixed roots are left unchanged rather than partially flattened.
